items.statement: TEA+–PC electronic binding relative to relaxed separated molecules
items.expected: An actual complete isolated gas-phase 1:1 TEA+–PC complex has negative electronic binding energy Eb = E(complex) − E(relaxed ion) − E(relaxed PC), with matched electronic method, charge, singlet state and energy convention. Report the computed value and units and establish the attractive sign at the claimed geometry. The numerical magnitude is supporting evidence for this sign, with no fixed target window. A frozen-fragment interaction energy or Gibbs energy is not this observable; a documented conversion to the relaxed-fragment electronic definition is admissible. Geometry, curvature and monomer identity validate the result without separate points. Copying a source value or comparing unmatched total energies fails.

items.statement: Relative local PC binding of DED2+ and BF4−
items.expected: Consistently defined relaxed-fragment electronic binding energies establish greater binding magnitude (more negative Eb) for DED2+–PC than BF4−–PC. Resolve this pairwise comparison using each complete ion and its own matched monomer reference at a common method and environment. Absolute total energies of differently charged complexes do not establish the result. This relative order is independent of whether all three association signs are established; source magnitudes are not fixed acceptance windows.

items.statement: Relative local PC binding of BF4− and TEA+

Resolve this independent pairwise comparison using complete ions, matched monomer references and a common method and environment. Do not award another result for reciting the full order; source magnitudes are not fixed acceptance windows.

items.statement: Conditional molecular explanation of the changed local PC environment
items.expected: Use actual association evidence and a composition/charge-balanced PC-transfer comparison, TEA·PC + DED → TEA + DED·PC or an equivalent energy cycle, to explain why adding DED can favor PC association near DED relative to TEA within the sampled local gas-phase baseline. The final scientific content is the conditional physical connection between a change in cation composition and competition for a finite local PC supply, not another point award for a pair ranking or the arithmetically derived transfer sign. Account for two BF4 per added DED salt unit and explain why independent 1:1 electronic energies do not fix solvent activities, many-body ion association, coordination populations or a concentration-dependent spectral trajectory. Tie that limit specifically to the supplied nonmonotonic observations; no bulk optimum or device inference follows. An equivalent well-supported conditional interpretation passes directly.
